My name is Elise & I am raising money for our animal shelter TripleA Marbella & San Pedro.
AAA - Amigos de Animales Abandonados (friends of the abandoned animals)
This year our charity celebrates 30 years of existence! We look after the abandoned animals in our municipality and currently we have over 500 animals in our care. The charity costs us over 600,000 € a year to stay open. 
Every day brings a new challenge and we cannot manage without our wonderful team of volunteers, members and donors. 
It is a heartbreaking journey, seeing animals malnourished, neglected, abused and unwanted. Money raised will be used to support our ongoing projects to make life better for these animals and you will receive updates on how your money is spent. 
Last year I walked 100,000 steps in a day for this cause and this year I will push myself a bit further, hopefully raise some much needed funds and spread awareness for TripleA. Please share, a small amount goes a long way to help our animals! 
Thank you so much x

What is Austin Pets Alive?
Hi! Want to join me in making a difference? My team and I are raising money to benefit Austin Pets Alive! Austin Pets Alive was first established in 1997 as a no-kill plan for all animals. Later on, in 2008, it became a rescue organization that assists animals in need by providing food, shelter, and medical support. This organization emphasizes decreasing the rate of euthanasia each year and is successfully doing so. In the previous 20 years, they have provided more than 20,000 surgeries for animals in need and are continuously growing.
Why is it important?
On average, 920,000 shelter animals are put down every year in the United States, Shelters around the world country put down an estimated 320,000 dogs and 600,000 cats each year. Between 4000 and 10,000 animals are euthanized daily. 9 out of 10 euthanized animals are adoptable and have no problems with them. 5 states are responsible for 51.5 percent of all animals euthanized. Texas is the second highest animal euthanized with 96.7. Texas euthanized a total of 15.5 percent of the total euthanized in the United States. The methods some shelters euthanized animals are carbon monoxide or carbon monoxide gas chambers. This method is sad because these animals are scared in the gas chambers, before passing away.
What is the process like to adopt? 
If you are thinking of adopting a pet it is an extremely easy process with Austin Pets Alive. A personal friend previously adopted a cat from Austin Pets Alive and this was the process she went through. “The process of adopting my cat Sadie was very easy. On the website, there is a catalog of animals of all types, sizes, sexes, and ages. Within this process, you are able to see pictures and videos of animals you are interested in and a brief description. You are also able to contact the fosters and shelters at any time. After contacting the shelter we adopted our cat Sadie over the phone within 10 minutes. Next, we went through a series of documents we were able to sign on the computer. A week later we were able to simply go and pick her up from her foster family.”
How can you help?
If you are an animal lover like us, help out this fantastic non-profit organization that adopts and fosters pets in the market by contributing to saving lives. There are many ways to help rescue these poor animals, but it all starts with your donations today! Your donations would go towards operations and medical support these animals need to survive. Thank you in advance for contributing to this cause which would mean the world to us.
More information about Austin Pets Alive!: To promote and provide the resources, education, and programs needed to eliminate the killing of companion animals.
Austin Pets Alive
P.O. Box 736245
Dallas, TX 75373-6245
Austin Pets Alive Website

Hi everyone, Our 4 month old German Shepard pup has had an accident and fractured her femur growth plate. Unfortunately this was very unexpected and could not have come at the worst time. We are asking out of the kindness of your heart to help us reach our goal in order to get our girl recovering, happy and healthy again. We are in all hopes  trying to avoid other harsh treatment options such as leg amputation. Our girl Sylvie is so young and has a lot of growing, playing , and exploring to do. Your contribution will be much appreciated and we also appreciate any and all support provided. This is a very difficult time and it breaks our hearts to see our girl go through this pain. Please help us get Sylvie the treatment she needs in order to lead a long and healthy and active life.

Hello everyone, this fundraiser is for Ozzy. My sweet 10 year old that suddenly has a decline in health. She has been undergoing testing at her main vet the last 2 months with a 2nd vet seeing her this last week. She had X-rays, ultrasounds and blood work ran without answers. She was prescribed antibiotics then steroids. No answers or diagnostic given during this period at all as nothing was showing on any of the tests unfortunately.  On October 30 she drastically declined, unable to walk, vomiting, difficulty breathing and lethargic. She was then taken to the ER and the moment they took her from my arms and to the back she went into cardiac arrest. Thankfully she was resuscitated. Additional tests were done and she was found to be septic from a previously unfound and untreated infection. She is currently on 24/7 oxygen, 24/7 IV antibiotics, 24/7 IV fluids and getting a blood transfusion. In addition more imaging and blood work is to be done once her vitals are hopefully more stable. She is currently, as of October 30 hospitalized for 48 hours with a reevaluation at the end of the 48 hours. I’ve never been in this position with one of my fur babies and any help or shares of this will be greatly appreciated. This sudden decline of health was extreamly unexpected and I truly hope to give her the best possible chance of recovery. My birthday is 11/05 and I want her still here with me for it. I will add the picture of the ER bill for the current visit shortly.

Hello fellow animal lovers! Every year our beloved local pet store, Critters & Co Pet Center, takes in hundreds of animals needing care and permanent placement. Some are found, some are quietly dropped off, and some are placed in coordination with their former owners. Regardless of how they arrive, they all need shelter, food, medical care and attention. In the ten months following our first GFM campaign (in November 2021) Debbie and her staff have taken in 458 animals.  FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY-EIGHT!!!  That's mind-blowing! That total includes 68 dogs, 74 cats, 44 guinea pigs, 1 snapping turtle, 8 ferrets, 16 chinchillas, 59 rabbits and a few hundred more of various mammals, birds, lizards, snakes, turtles, and more! 
This year the need is greater than ever. As people return to work and life circumstances change, animals continue to be surrendered at increasing rates. Additionally, inflation has negatively impacted all of us, including Critters & Co and their efforts to care for these animals. 
My co-organizer, Elizabeth, and I thank you for taking the time read about this campaign. We would also greatly appreciate 1) donations of any amount, and 2) please share this campaign! 
About 1 in 5 who review this campaign will donate, which means we need to get this to at least 1,000 people to have a reasonable chance of reaching our goal of $14,000.  
Thank you in advance to our generous and wonderful community!

Hi my name is Paige and I am opening up this go fund me for my pretty puppy Keisha! Keisha is a 4.5 year old pure bread Sheltie. Keisha came into my life when she was 3 months old. She stole my heart from the moment I saw her. I knew it was love at first sight! She is and has been the most amazing pup! At 1 years old she suffered an awful seizure which was absolutely devastating!!! Within the last year she has suffered more than 5 seizure! In March of 2022 she was put on phenobarbital to control her seizures but they keep happening. Mommy and daddy are completely heart broken. Keisha doesn't deserve this! My mommy has decided to get me help through a neurologist!! Keisha's appointment is scheduled for November 10th. The first visit is an automatic $300. Keisha will have to go through an MRI and or CT scan which could cost upward of $10,000 dollars! Doesn't matter how big or how small. If you can not donate we understand times are rough and if you could just share this we would greatly appreciate it!!! Keisha deserves this and we will do that it takes to make her quality of life that much better!!! Thank you from the bottom of our hearts!!!!

Hi my name is Salem and I have a 9 month old puppy named maize. She has had a severe skin allergy resulting in complete hair loss on her lower back and tail, an ear infection, and infected sores on her armpits and belly from itching. Hi my name is Gina and I am trying to raise funds for our sweet baby boy Winston the pug. I got Winston from a breeder named honey pets. Winston’s adoption day kept getting pushed back stating that Winston wasn’t ready to leave his mom and that he was still to little and not cleared by the vet for adoption! Once I got Winston he had a little hacking cough which at the time I thought it was nothing, this poor baby developed bilateral meaning both and all lung lobes pneumonia. Winston has been on iv antibiotics, iv fluids and in an oxygen cage. I am so heart broken and am at the max of what I could afford to continue his treatment but he deserves to live! If you could please find it in your heart to donate to this beautiful baby boy as my son and myself have fallen in love with him  so much and he deserves to live! Please help us save Winston!!

Hi, my name is Robin and I need your help. I am raising funds to save Mr. Whiskers life. Mr. Whiskers was adopted in June of 2018 for my daughter Kyra. With having just moved clear across country from the only home she has ever known, Kyra was struggling to make a home for herself in Florida, let alone make any friends. Mr. Whiskers has been there for her every day of that journey and now is time for us to help him. Mr. Whiskers is fighting for his life with FIP (feline infectious peritonitis). There are treatments for this deadly disease, but that is where we need help. The cost of vet bills and treatment are a lot. So the money donated will go strictly for that. Please help me save my daughter’s best friend.

I am disabled and on a limited income. I started his first month of treatment but I cannot afford to continue treatment after this month. I'm asking for help to save this baby's life and give him a chance at a long life and knowing what it's like to be loved and part of a family

It has been painful to watch the events unfold in the world. We show our support by flying the blue and yellow flag or boldly displaying the blue and yellow colors to show there’s strength in unity. Still, many of us wish we could do more. But how? There are animals in need of evacuation but lack the funding and means to do so. We have been working with Robert, a dedicated veterinarian, in hopes of saving some of these poor, forgotten souls left to fend for themselves. This is the harrowing story of a homeless litter of puppies and their mom as they struggle to survive amid a war-torn nation. A stray dog had a litter of 9 puppies on the streets of Kharkiv during the intense shelling in mid-August. In an outrageous act of callousness, a man entombed our mother alive in a concrete basement, sealing off any exits and the fate of my 3 siblings. However, Robert and his team came to their rescue, demolishing the concrete wall and bringing the mama dog and 6 surviving puppies to his clinic where they could recover. Because the mother dog was very weak, she didn’t have enough milk to feed her babies. So Robert selflessly bottle-fed them every 2 hours day and night. He stayed away from his own family to be with them in the clinic 24/7. But they have no future there, at least for now. To transport each one to NY will cost us $800. So with your generous donations, we hope to raise enough to fly 3 puppies (to start) to America, where we can show them the loving, safe life they truly deserve. Would you please help us save these innocent lives?

My name is Courtney. Our family owns WBARMINDIANA. We not only ride horses recreationally but WE HAVE SAVED 4 horses from slaughter this year from Indiana to Ohio to Kentucky to Texas. After we pick up the horses, we bring them back to our farm, quarantine, get them vetted & ridable to rehome. We also keep in touch with the new owners. However….
 We had a devastating accident with our rig & our trailer is totaled with no insurance. Only comprehensive on our truck. On our way to pick up a rescue. ….We plan to continue to rescue horses from slaughter starting back in February or sooner. We do not have the funds for even a used trailer to haul them & we recently found out that the roadside recovery will NOT BE COVERED AT ALL BY ANY INSURANCE, including environmental clean up. We are raising funds to help recover from this tragic accident & hopefully get WBARMINDIANA on the road again in the spring. Thank you

My name is Sara and I am fundraising for this little guy, Walter. He was found last summer wandering around Arizona in triple digit heat. He was abandoned and left to fend for himself. He’s got terrible arthritis, his hairs are a mess- but he’s Walter. He has overcome everything bad that’s ever happened to him and is the most resilient and happy little dude I have ever met. He never complains about anything. Which is why we didn’t realIze the mat on his tail was hiding an infection- we have no idea what happened to cause it. He is at the emergency vet right now, getting his butt shaved and the wound irrigated. We will use any funds collected to cover his ER costs and any follow-up care that he will need. This animal is a special being that deserves to be happy and healthy for the rest of his life. Any help is appreciated. Thank you!!

It feels strange to ask for help, but someone pointed out that we all like to help a good cause, and this sweet boy sure could use it.  
Last night we rescued this dog from a home in which the owners just WERE NOT FEEDING HIM… for months.. weeks… his whole life?  Possibly.  We got him to the vet first thing this morning and his rapt sheet of diagnoses is daunting to say the least.  
• He is extremely emaciated and malnourished.  He’s a Great Dane/lab mix and weighed in at only 53 pounds.  
• His white blood cell count is 4x what is should be due to a raging bacterial infection
• He came in with a fever of 105.6 due to the bacterial infection. 
• His platelet count is dangerously low-a potential fatal problem 
• His electrolytes are depleted from malnutrition
•He could barely get around and couldn’t even stand for any period of time
• And lastly, and maybe the most gut-wrenching diagnosis, his HEART HAS SHRUNK due to extreme dehydration. 
I know you’re thinking, my God, WTF is wrong with people?!  Believe me, we are too. But we have to focus our energy on this good boy and what we can do for him. There is HOPE!  He spent the day with the vet getting pumped full of liquids and medicine and all the care and the difference in his spirits and his appetite are giving us, and the medical staff, a lot of hope that he’s going to pull through!  His little heart will swell back to normal with time and fluids.  Antibiotics are battling the infection and anti inflammatories have brought his temperature down to normal.  We were so so happy to hear that he started eating again once his fever subsided!  Last night when we picked him up his appetite was shockingly non-existent and we thought he might have just given up.  He has decidedly perked up in the past 24 hours and we are very hopeful!  
This boy is so so sweet despite being treated so horribly.  He is just a big bucket of love. All of the staff at the vets office are already attached to him and they commented on how sweet he was despite feeling so awful.  
Hes not out of the woods yet but he is trying and has made good progress in the past 24 hours.  We have total faith one day he will be a nice healthy weight and will be able to run and play on the farm just like our girl Molly does.  The two of them are getting along fabulously and shared a bed last night <3 
If you feel moved to do so, please help us help this sweet boy get all better.  We definitely had no plans on getting a second dog when we woke up yesterday morning, let alone one that would need so much medical care, but what can you do?  
Thank you guys so much for any amount, big or small!  It means a lot of us and to all the neglected dogs out there!

Hi, my name is Joselyn. I'm a mother of two small children. My kids begged for a dog for so long so my husband and I decided to adopt Luna in April. We've loved her and played with her so much. She become a huge part of our family. However, on November 10th we noticed Luna was no longer eating, drinking or going to the bathroom. She sleeps all day and her energy has drastically decreased. We took her to the vet and was told that she is suffering from kidney failure. It is only a matter of time before she passes. Unless she gets the treatment that she needs. Unfortunately my family and I cannot afford it and would appreciate the help. Thank you so much for taking the time to read this.

After bringing her to the emergency vet they needed a deposit of $3,800 just to keep her over night and another $1,200 to start a diagnosis. My dear friends, Shad and Lourdes Ross, had their fur baby, Logan, get hit by a car. The car drove off, not stopping to offer any aid.
Logan has had an operation to save his leg. The cost will be $5,500. The funds you donate will pay for Logan's operation and any additional medical care.
God bless.

Hi neighbors! My name is Haley and I live on Linden street in Livermore California( we have the giving tree out front) I feed and trap the neighborhood strays independently with no rescue backing and have spayed/ neutered 15 so far. I have also adopted out 8 of the friendly ones. It now costs me $180 per cat as the discounted clinic I go to in Hayward has raised their prices and up until now I have paid all the costs out of my own pocket. I have tried other discounted clinics but cannot seem to find one with weekend availability ( I work full time) and usually they are booked months and months out. I have 5 cats and 1 dog myself and am starting to get overwhelmed with handling the spay costs on my own. Some of the cats I’ve taken to the vet have been diagnosed with FELV which is a very contagious disease that can be passed from the mother to the kittens and from one stray to another. So the sooner we can stop the reproducing, the better. I’m hoping to have the entire colony spayed by the start of the kitten season next year. No donation is too small, even if you donate $1 it will help. I have an appointment next Saturday to get two fixed and I would gladly send the vet receipts for anyone that is thinking about donating so you can have peace of mind that your money is going to the animals in need and not for my personal gain. Please see the go fund me link below, thank you so much for reading! Also would love any advice from others independents/ rescues that do TNR in Alameda county on where they go and how they afford it.

On October 10th I found destiny half dead at the local shelter. I rushed her to the vet and they told me she needed a $1300 blood transfusion to live. I didn't have the money so I brought her home to at least get her warm and fed. I made a tiktok in the parking lot crying and so many wonderful people stepped up and donated over 6k so that Destiny could get the care she needed to survive. She defied the odds and after 5 days in the ER she came home and was doing great.  She stayed with me until November 9th when she went to her forever home with Brie and Wesley. 
Today on November 13th I got a call from Brie that Destiny is back in the ER with an enlarged kidney about to burst any minute.  She needs to see a specialist immediately to have it removed which will cost 10k and she's already racked up 5k in tests and supportive care at the ER vet. I know it's a huge ask, but if everyone who follows me could donate $15 we could save Destiny once again and hopefully for the last time! 
I thought about not telling you guys and just letting her go with grace, but I know you would want to know and help if you can. 
Thank you for reading. Hug your babies tight for me

Hi. My name is Donna Magtibay. I am helping Danelle Magtibay and Craig Harting raise funds to bring a service dog named Walter home for their son, Shaun. Shaun has autism, ASD Level 3 and requires substantial support. He has a limited ability to interact socially with others, and his communication is assisted using a specialized computer. He also has a seizure disorder.
Service dogs are expensive and worth every penny. Walter is being explicitly trained to meet Shaun's special needs, including the ability to detect a seizure. When a person has a seizure, their body emits a unique scent that a trained service dog can detect up to ten minutes in advance. Walter will be trained to detect this scent and alert Shaun's parents, who can then work together with Walter to keep Shaun safe. Walter will also help increase Shaun's independence and keep him safe while doing daily activities in the community, such as going to a park, shopping, or walking in the neighborhood. People with autism often feel isolated. Walter will become Shaun's best friend and a bridge to the world around him.
We thank you so much for your donations. If we go over our goal, that money will be used for further service training and expenses needed to keep Walter healthy and happy.
Wishing you many blessings,
Danelle Magtibay and Craig Harting 
Donna Magtibay

First of all I appreciate your kind support and so does Nova. Nova is a 4 year old husky, golden retriever mix with a heart of gold. Otherwise very healthy and happy she suddenly fell ill this week. Unfortunately I’m currently unable to work due to my own physical and mental issues so at this time I’m unable to help my loving dog. It breaks my heart to see my energetic pup unable to get up. She hasn’t eaten in days and is unfortunately taking a turn for the worse. Please help me and Nova, thank you!

Hi. My name is Cara and I am starting a fundraiser for our dear friend Katryn Schmidt and her beloved pets. On October 21st, Katryn's rent house burned down while she was at work. A faulty water heater. The firefighters responded quickly and were able to rescue her dog and two cats. Unfortunately, the smoke inhalation was too much for her dog Charlie to overcome. After 48 hours of veterinary treatment he passed away.
Her two cats, Swinky and LaRue are doing okay. They are still being treated as they are not eating or drinking after such a traumatic event.
If you know Katryn, you know that her animals mean the world to her. Even after losing everything, her biggest concern is her babies. The vet bills are extensive and ongoing. She has rescued countless animals and has paid for vet visits, vaccinations, spaying and neutering, heartworm treatments, and surgeries before finding them good homes. She has saved the lives of dozens of animals that have gone on to bring such joy to their new families.
As a community, I'd like for us to come together to help out our friend and her precious pets. Any donation would be appreciated and would go to the veterinary bills. Anything left over will go towards buying the things the cats will need after losing everything.

Aunt Heidi loved animals, took in 2 rescue dogs and fed the feral cats in her neighborhood. May her love for animals and her desire to keep them safe continue on. Please donate to this vital charity.
More information about McCook Humane Society: Since 1983 the McCook Humane Society has provided a temporary home for puppies and kittens, as well as adult dogs and cats. They are dedicated to finding permanent, loving homes for abused, neglected, and abandoned animals in Southwest Nebraska and Northwest Kansas.
McCook Humane Society

Please consider donating to support the effort to find sheltie, Halle, who went missing in Norcross, GA on October 24, 2022. All funds will be managed by the Shetland Sheepdog Club of Georgia and be distributed to cover costs associated with the search such as flyers, posters, yard signs, live traps, bait, food and water for volunteers. Any left over funds collected will be donated to the Sheltie Rescue of Georgia to support the Shetland Sheepdog Breed.

Hi, my name is Cora Hartigan, and I am currently raising money to complete the heartworm treatment of a shelter dog named Bruce. Bruce is a very sweet and loving dog that is currently at Marion County Animal Shelter in SC. He was picked up and brought to the shelter with little known about his history. I had the pleasure of meeting him while volunteering at the shelter and fell absolutely in love with him. I even got to give him the name bruce. At $500, Heartworm treatments are very costly and a long process, so the shelter needs resources to help fund his treatment. Bruce is one of many dogs with heartworms out of the shelter's 100+ dogs. Heartworm disease is a serious and potentially fatal disease in pets in the United States and many other parts of the world. It is caused by foot-long worms (heartworms) that live in the heart, lungs and associated blood vessels of affected pets, causing severe lung disease, heart failure and damage to other organs in the body. Left untreated, this poor baby could potentially lose his life. The treatment process includes a series of injections followed by a month-long period of rest and limited exercise. Having this treatment gives bruce a great chance of being adopted and finally living the life he deserves. Any donations will help. Thank you for your kindness.

Hi, I'm Sara, a volunteer at Dekalb County Animal Services. This sweet, young pup, Buttery Biscuit, needs some help to see better days: She was found by Animal Enforcement tied up to a building a few days ago with infections, swelling in the groin, and in overall poor condition. As of 11/07/22, she is unable to pee on her own and vets believe something more serious may be in the way. Until and unless a rescue is able to pull her, her situation remains dire without more immediate diagnosis and treatment.  This fundraiser is to support the immediate intervention needed to diagnose Buttery Biscuit’s underlying medical issues and address them. Thank you so much for helping out! Please donate what you're able or share this fundraiser to help this sweet girl!

Hi, my name is Bricia. I am setting up this GoFundMe for my mother's cat, Cali. On Tuesday, October 4th, 2022, we took Cali to Bluepearl Monterey, considering that he had an apparent injury to the face. Cali had been missing for two days before returning home, which is very unlikely of him. Subsequently, after receiving care from the surgeon team at Bluepearl, a CT scan revealed that Cali's jaw had been broken on the right side and the joint area where the left jaw connects to the skull. The surgeon team believes Cali was hit by a car or was caused by blunt force trauma. The cause of injuries crushed a bit of the upper mount and caused some blood clotting in the nasal cavity. Out of all injuries sustained, the surgeon had said Cali would have a bit of a recovery time but would be able to heal fully and have a healthy life. 
The surgeon who took care of Cali at Bluepearl Monterey referred us to Dentistry for Animals in Aptos, considering that they would be able to assist Cali with his "maxillofacial trauma" further.  Animals of Dentistry was a great help. They performed the necessary procedure for the maxillofacial trauma and put Cali on a feeding tube to get the required nutrients during his recovery. 
My mother is not working; therefore, when I took charge of taking my mother's cat to the emergency vet, they told me Cali could live everyday life. I right away gave my care credit card to Bluepearl and Dentistry for Animals. Thanks to Carecredit, we could help Cali with the necessary help, but it resulted in me using $9,263.29. This does not include aftercare when they take out wires and redo X-rays to ensure he is healing correctly in a few weeks. 
I ask the community's HELP to help me pay the Carecredit fees I am now responsible for. Any amount you can spare to help me pay the credit? It would be greatly appreciated. It's been a crazy two weeks, and Cali is recovering finely. 
I'll share some before and after pictures to follow our journey with Cali.

On October 31st, Sagan needed to be rushed to the emergency vet as she was extremely lethargic, struggling to stand and unable to eat. After countless diagnostic tests, she needed a life-saving blood transfusion, as her red blood cell count was extremely low. Sagan was suffering from severe anemia in addition to liver failure. She’s currently under observation and may need an additional transfusion while hospitalized. The cause of Sagan’s sudden illness is still being determined. Until her test results return, the veterinarian is hesitant to give us a clear idea about her chance of full recovery. Her red blood cell count is struggling to stabilize, but we’re hoping the treatment will continue to work with the slight improvement they’ve seen.
To anyone who knows Mike, Sagan is almost constantly by his side. Since the first time she jumped into his car out of the blue they’ve been out on the roads, on the trails, or out hanging around town living life. There’s never a person that Sagan doesn’t rush up to greet with her charming enthusiasm. Her positive energy is contagious among us.
This unexpected emergency has been overwhelming, and both Mike and Sagan could use a helping hand. Sagan’s veterinarian bill has already surpassed $7,800, and it’s expected to rise as her complete treatment plan gets worked out. We’re still unsure what the cause of her illness is, but we know that she will need immune suppressant drugs to support her body once the blood transfusions are complete. 
Sagan may not have much bark in her (right now), but she’s a fighter. Anything you can contribute to help Sagan continue the treatment she’s receiving, heal and recuperate is greatly appreciated. We’ll share updates on Sagan’s battle, and please share this so that the word spreads.

Yesterday, my four-year-old service dog Phoenix sadly got into my medications and chocolate on my nightstand. I am dependent on her for a lot of my daily needs. She is more than just a service dog to me. She has become a member of my family; I don't know what I would do without her. She’s currently in Bulger Veterinary Hospital. Her current bill is $3500. I need help. The next few hours are critical and will determine the length of her stay and rehabilitation. I don’t have anybody who could help; it would greatly be appreciated. God bless you all.

OnFriday, October 21, 2022 Cindy Smith and her Chihuahua Katana were mauled by another dog in Leisurewood where both were injured.  Katana's injuries were life threatening consisting of numerous lacerations  1 required staples, 1 lost tooth, 2 cracked ribs, 2 broken ribs and a perforated lung. On the island:
$1 can deworm a pup.
$5 can provide flea & tick medicine.
$10 can get a dog to the vet.
$15 can feed an adult dog for a month.
$21 can feed a puppy for a month.
You could save a life for less than the cost of a Starbucks drink. Could you please spare a dollar or perhaps more?

In a tropical forest in Southern India, a conflict between monkeys and the humans that live alongside them has been ongoing for decades. These monkeys risk electrocution, poisoning, auto accidents, and attacks by street dogs simply living their daily lives; yet the humans living mere meters away remain unaware. In order to understand the lives of these complex social creatures and develop ways to conserve one of the most diverse ecosystems on earth, researchers have been studying monkey behavior in a town called Thenmala since 2019. I am asking for your support to continue one of the longest studies of bonnet macaques in India, and the longest running study of this species in the wild.
I am a researcher and editor with a background in ecology. I am raising funds on behalf of Dr. Malgorzata Arlet (Poland) who works in collaboration with Professor Mewa Singh (India) and Professor Lynne Isbell (USA). I am a project associate as a fundraiser and grant writer. 
All proceeds of this fundraiser go directly to the Thenmala Macaque Project, which focuses on the behavior and conservation of bonnet macaques living in and around the Thenmala Ecotourism Center in Kerala, India. Please scroll to the end for information on how this money will be spent and how money will be transferred from this fundraiser to the Principal Investigator.*  No raffles, sweepstakes, giveaways, or returns on investment are offered in exchange for any donations made to this GoFundMe.
Who are these monkeys?
Bonnet macaques are a species of monkey that weigh around 9-14 pounds in adulthood, eat fruits, nuts, and insects, and live 20-25 years in the wild. They are highly social, living in communities called ‘troops’ of around 30 members, where they collectively raise their young, form bonds and hierarchies, and even form coalitions to fight for who leads the troop. They form matrilineal societies, meaning the highest ranking female leads the troop, and it is common for the daughter or granddaughter of a matriarch to take charge when the matriarch dies. Bonnet macaques have been seen adopting infants whose mothers have died, and there is evidence that mothers may grieve for lost infants and close relatives.
Even though their troops are matrilineal, males in the troop form coalitions and a power structure of their own, which determines who their mating partners will be, who leads the defense of the troop, and which males are allowed to become a part of the troop. When males born in a troop mature, they find a new troop to live with, whereas females stay with their troop their entire lives.
What is the conflict?
Human-monkey conflict is widespread in India. As the human population grows, so does its need for resources and space. This results in a loss of habitat for monkeys as it is transformed to meet the demands of people. Moreover, increased human population results in higher vehicular traffic and infrastructure such as power lines. In Thenmala, there are numerous accidents where monkeys were fatally hit by vehicles or electrocuted, both of which occur while the monkeys navigate their range using roads and electric wires. There are also deaths due to choking on plastic and suspected poisonings either due to human negligence or intent. From February 2020 to October 2021 alone, 30 of the 47 infants born in the two troops the research team study died, most due to human-monkey conflict. Five infants were orphaned, and only one, named ‘Thor’, continues to survive in the absence of his mother.
Muscan is an infant whose left hand is paralyzed, likely due to electrocution. Injuries like this make it more difficult for the infant to hold onto their mother or move, affecting their chances of survival.
In addition to fatalities, some individuals lose limbs or tails from electrocution, which often results in a struggle for that individual to survive. The presence of humans in macaque habitats can also result in a dietary shift, as monkeys are forced to forage for human food, which may result in poorer health. This foraging can cause resentment in the humans living in these settlements, and intentional poisonings have been observed in other macaque species at other sites.
Noyong is an infant with an infection in their right hand. Aside from limiting mobility, the infection poses a serious risk to Noyong's life. The cause of Noyong's injury is unknown, but infections after electrocution injuries are common.
Bonnet macaques are considered ‘vulnerable’ by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, meaning that unless locals find ways to coexist with these monkeys, they are at risk of becoming endangered and one day extinct. Studying a species that is not yet endangered allows this research group to understand the reasons for their decline and how best to conserve them before it is too late to reverse the damage caused.
Why is this location so important?
The Thenmala Ecotourism Center is the first ecotourism center in India. The role of ecotourism centers is to allow visitors to experience rare or endangered ecosystems and learn about the importance of conserving these areas in a way that is safe for both wildlife and visitors. Thenmala Ecotourism Center provides guided tours across walkways that prevent damage to the ecosystem and provide protection from the multiple species of venomous snakes and other dangerous wildlife. They also offer classes, activities, and events that teach visitors about the unique animal and plant life found in the region, as well as how they can help preserve such a rare and unique environment.
Built near an existing town and reservoir, this site has historically been a location of conflict between humans and monkeys. While the ecotourism center aims to mitigate this conflict, it persists, mainly to the detriment of the monkeys. By studying bonnet macaques in this setting, the research group is able to not only study mother-infant interactions in the context of human-monkey conflict but also support the mission of the Thenmala Ecotourism Center by providing insight into how effective their conservation efforts are and develop new conservation methods.
What does the research team want to do?
One of the most important bonds formed in bonnet macaques is between a mother and her infant. While this bond is strongest during the first few weeks of life, it persists for 6-10 months until the infant is weaned. This relationship is where infants learn to forage, avoid threats, form social bonds, and heavily influences the social circles the infants will be a part of as adults. While the primary aim of the project has been to study maternal care and personality development of infants, an increase in human-animal conflict in recent years has led the research team to focus on conservation.
Through the money raised from this fundraiser, the researchers aim to construct canopy bridges across high-traffic areas and power lines that will allow monkeys to move from one place to another with little risk. Additionally, they will conduct educational workshops for residents in collaboration with the local Forest Department to raise awareness about the importance of conserving this vulnerable species.
Lastly, these funds allow the researchers to continue behavioral data collection on mothers and infants to better understand the role of human stressors on the reproduction of female monkeys and the mortality of their infants. Long-term studies such as this allow them to answer many more questions than any individual study can. With years of data from an ongoing study, they can look at large-scale and long-term patterns, which provide insights into new conservation measures and how to deploy current conservation efforts most effectively.
What does your money do?
This fundraiser goal will:
- Fund 2 research assistants and a project manager to continue their research for six months.**
- Provide the materials, labor, and installation for ten canopy bridges, which will be installed strategically to minimize accidents due to electrocution and vehicle collisions.
- Support four community workshops to educate residents and visitors about the importance of conservation efforts to protect bonnet macaques.
Any funds received over the goal will be strategically applied to maximize the benefits of research and conservation efforts:
- $1,052 will fund the research team for an additional month
- $80 will fund one additional canopy bridge
- $50 will fund one additional community workshop
If donors significantly exceed the fundraiser goal, the research team plans to hire additional researchers and expand the scope of their experiment to additional troops.***

Trials have shown that GS-441524 has promising results with most cats making a full recovery after treatment, and some improvements in symptoms within only a few days after treatment begins. However, time is important and treatments need to begin before the disease progresses too far. There are several vets in Calgary and all over that are supportive of FIP treatments and will help support cats as they undergo treatment. The treatment is very costly, unfortunately. 
Ozzy is my absolute world, my best friend, and my emotional support.  Ozzy and I need help fighting - he needs and deserves a chance - before it's too late. FIP is a cruel monster of a disease that takes the lives of way too many of our feline companions while they are much too young. Neither Ozzy nor I are ready to part ways in this lifetime, we've still got so many more memories to make together. He needs your help to stay with his family and live out a healthy life.
Any donations would be greatly appreciated and 100% of donations would go to getting Ozzy the medicine he needs, which I will be privately ordering through an incredible organization that fights to put an end to the death sentence that is FIP. Please help make Ozzy and FIP warrior and success story.

Hi we are Reese and Christine farmers/owners of GoneStraw Farms.
We are a husband and wife team specializing in fantastic eggs. We started over 10 years ago as a hobby quickly morphing into a lifestyle. We started with 20 chicks over a decade ago as something fun to do with the kids. Then grew to 500 in our small backyard selling to neighbors and farmers markets. Through a freind we found out that a large poultry farm was shutting down their operation. We were blessed to have gotten a meeting with the wonderful owner of the property, and he agreed to let this crazy couple attempt their dream of becoming full time poultry farmers. And because of this opportunity to lease this poultry ranch we have been able to realize that dream of living this wonderful life as farmers. Over the years we have had some rough patches. Its not for the faint of heart for sure! Enduring a newcastle outbreak in 2018 having the government destroy all our feathered friends on the farm and only giving us 1 cent per bird nearly bankrupting us with their treatment and demands. We somehow push through that and started gaining ground on expanding our delivery business to then have it completely wiped out by the pandemic. Shifting our focus to our eggstand out in front of the farm and developing a home delivery route was our saving grace. All while dealing with a constant seemingly a nightly or weekly theft issue on the backside of our farm. We have been robbed too many times to mention out back and in the chicken houses. It has become something we deal with. It goes along with finding and keeping hired hands around. We have always known this place would someday be sold off to a developer and we would get our walking papers, but that is now becoming a reality with a new very big housing development going in right next door and it will be consuming our location as well. So we have been trying to plan for that with a little saving and planning for our next location to permanently root ourselves in our community to continue the wonderful relationships and service to our neighbors. We love sharing our lifestyle with all those who are curious. And finally, we just recently experienced our first home invasion last Sunday October 30, 2022 at 3 in the afternoon. They snuck past our egg stand lady and entered our home in broad daylight. We think they were looking for the stand money. They stumble across our feed money and our nest egg. Not only is our ability to feed our birds been catastophically effected but our funds to help us make our next jump to a new farm location is gone. We will continue no matter what pushing forward but not sure what that looks like. We love and appreciate all our customers and look forward to providing our local community with the most eggcellent eggs.

In the early morning hours (1 am) of October 16th , while sitting around the fire with some friends, we noticed a white pickup truck pull into the paddock area of NCCAR. This is a racetrack in a remote area of Garysburg, NC. Vehicles coming in and out isn’t uncommon during an event, so we didn’t pay much attention at first. 
After a while, one of the truck’s doors opened and a dog hopped out. It began to trot around smelling the area like most dogs would do. After inspecting for a minute or so, it started to head back to the truck’s open door, but before it could get back in, the door closed. As the truck pulled away, the dog chased it, crying. At this point, we realized that the person/persons were abandoning this poor animal on this cold 40ish-degree night. The truck sped off into the night out the main gates as the dog trotted around wondering where they were going without her. We coaxed the dog over to see if we could help. We got her some water and decided to make a bed for her in our warm RV for the evening until the morning when we would find some help for her.
Sunday morning, after a nights rest, a few of us began to care for her, getting food, more water, and some type of collar/leash. With racecars zipping around we were afraid she would be hit. We tried to see if it was a mistake and the owners were there, but unfortunately, this wasn’t the case. I contacted my wife who was at our home in Sanford, NC, and told her of the situation. She began to try to contact the local no-kill shelters, rescues, and even the Northhampton Sheriffs' office. Unfortunately, nobody could help until Monday. At this point, nobody could take the dog or wait until Monday to bring her somewhere. My wife and I decided that I would take her home that evening and we could get her some help. She is a very sweet, well-mannered dog. She had some snacks, took some walks, and a few naps while she waited for me to finish my morning and get packed up to head home.
When I arrived home, we got her some toys, flea treatment, and a good meal. Our current dog and two cats seemed to like her and there were no issues between them. Once we realized that it wasn’t going to be an issue with our current animals, we wanted to have the dog checked out and potentially decide on what we were going to do. We took her to the vet on the morning of October 18th. Unfortunately, this sweet girl has heartworms, Lyme Disease, and Ehrlichia from her previous miss care. We were able to get her vaccinations up to date and scan for a microchip (no luck).
Lynn and I have created this GoFundMe to raise some funds so that we can get the treatment she needs. The treatment process is about 6 months long and costs over $2,000. We will be applying this to her heartworm treatment, spaying, and some of the other miscellaneous costs associated (antibiotics, overnight stay, etc.). Our hope is to make her a permanent fixture in our family but if that doesn’t work after the 6 months for any reason, we feel this will give her the best chance of getting adopted.

Hello everyone. My name is Ron but I am sure most of you have seen Chester in my social media stories and feeds as I have pretty much evolved from a dog lover to a full-time cat dad. But what most of you did not know is this little fellow's insane backstory.
Chester was born on October 31st, 2017, behind my restaurant in Artesia. It wasn't until New Year's Eve on December 31st, 2017, that my customer brought Chester to me. At first, we thought that he was scared, but it turned out he was paralyzed. Many of my friends and family warned that I would be in for a wild ride if I decided to take him in, but despite all the warnings, we grew close, and with the love and care I poured into him, he started to recover and learned how to walk and run once again three months later. We still do not know what caused this issue, but we suspect it might be some tick infection, combined with his genetic makeup, that caused it.
Fast forward to May 15, 2019, Chester was spooked by a dog and ran off; we couldn't find the little fellah for the longest time. Chester would go missing for another 2 years before we miraculously came across him in our neighborhood. What's even crazier is that we found him on the morning of Nov. 1st of, 2021, a day after his birthday. Many people, including myself, thought that he would had no chance after being gone for so long. But despite the odds stacked against us, we were reunited.
Yesterday, October 31st, 2022, on Chester's 5th birthday, I rushed him to Orangethrope Animal Aid Hospital. At first, I thought he was feeling under the weather and might have caught the flu as he was having difficulty breathing. In the lobby, while we were waiting, Chester started coughing out liquid and blood. Other waiting patients began to help and clear space for Chester as he was going into a seizure state. He stabilized 5 minutes later, thanks to everyone and the team at Orangethrope Animal Aid Hospital. We immediately began transferring to a more extensive, special care facility - Fountain Valley/West Coast VCA under the advice of our family vet at Orangethrope Animal Aid.
Both facilities broke the news to me that Chester was found to have liquids in his lungs and heart, and that his heart is enlarged and he suffers a type of heart problem we called RCM (Restricted Cardiomyopathy). This means that his heart muscle has thickened, and he has problems pumping blood. The doctor informed me that he had been recovering slowly but surely after an overnight stay. However, it is recommended that he stay another night tonight to completely drain his fluid and keep him in the oxygen room for another night. They informed me that it's very likely that Chester will be on medication for the rest of his life. To top it off, they told me that cats that suffer from heart failure usually has about 6-12 months to live, but there are cases where the cats continue to live a good life after that period.
I have been a pet owner my entire life and never had a significant issue with my pets like this. I have dug into my savings, and I would be lying if I said I was not exhausted by this new revelation for the past few days. I couldn't say no to the birthday boy, to the cat that's been through hell with me and back and through the worst time of my life. The least I can do is suck up my ego and seek for help.
I know times are tough, so I appreciate any help. Whether it be donation, or spread the word for me.
We had odds stacked against us before, and we prevailed. This is no different. We have proven this to everyone before, and I am sure we can do it again.
Thanks for your time <3
- Ron

Azeez Story: My name is Azeez and I am a 23 year old Yazidi student from Sinjar in Iraq. I am a UWC Adriatic 2021 alumn, and currently a freshman at St. Olaf college in Minnesota-USA.In 2014, Iraq and my city specifically Sinjar went through a crisis due to the attacks by ISIS, and resulting in the full control over my city by ISIS. Hence, resulting in the Yazidi genocide, which happened on the 3rd of August, 2014.  Like other people from my minority we had to escape to the mountain since my city was completely occupied by ISIS except the mountain. My family, and I had to escape to the mountain. We survived there for nine days without any food and water, or anything we owned. We were eating leaves and drinking the rainwater stored in caves. It was truly an unfortunate situation. I observed heartbreaking scenes, I saw friends and relatives being killed, dying of thirst and starvation, people crying, frightened by the bullet shots over us. We were close to losing the hope to continue in life, until we escaped to northern Iraq. We were kept in plastic tents for more than 5 years and it has been like that since then.  My home and most of my hometown were destroyed. Specifically, the house that my parents worked on building their lives, was bombed and left to ashes during the occupation. After five years, we went back to our city in the hopes that our government would rebuild it. We were residing in a house that did not belong to us because the previous owners had left Iraq. As a result, after the city's situation began to improve and numerous organisations began to visit, people began renting out the remaining houses. As a result, the owner asked my family to leave the home and granted them two months to do so, a while ago. Meaning, my family and I are at a loss as to what to do since we have nowhere else to live. Especially since living in tents would be extremely difficult due to the incoming harsh winter in the north of Iraq. But I didn't give up. I made a pledge to my parents, who are both ill in Iraq and are unable to work, to finish my studies and work hard to achieve their dreams. I started working the maximum number of hours on campus, despite the fact that it is interfering with my studies since I do not have excellent mental health, but I am doing everything I can to help them, and it is not working. Therefore, I need your help to get my family a place to live while I continue my study.

After opening her apartment door, the smoke from the hallway rushed into her apartment, and she knew she was in trouble. Without knowing what was waiting for her on the staircase, she ran through the smoke, unable to breathe or see anything. By a miracle, Leslie made it out of the fire without any significant injuries.
Leslie made it out with her phone and the clothes on her body, but everything else was gone. In the fire, she lost all her most sentimental items, clothes, a computer, and other things that can't be replaced. Amongst it all, her brand-new car was one of the first things to burn on the ground floor of the apartment complex. She only had her car for a week before losing it, and her insurance company cannot cover her loss. So, Leslie needs a lot of help to rebuild, and we're hoping there's a community around her that can make that happen. Thank you to everyone!

I said to John, shouldn’t we take the RV inland to our friend’s house.
No, even if there is a surge it’s not going to be that high.
THE PLAN
Park the RV in our driveway, which is protected facing north between our house and the neighbor’s house.
Stock enough essentials to last a few days
Check the onboard generator
Fill gas tank
Fill water tank
Watch the weather news
Honker down in the RV which is taller than the house and wait
REALITY
Watched the weather news
8-12 ft. Water surge was possible but our area has a number of little islands of mangroves that should have detoured it
North of us in Bonita Shores in Bonita Springs was getting hammered because of the bands on the north side of Ian
Not much was happening
Water started to flood the back yard
Things were floating in the back yard
Rising pretty quickly it started to come in the RV
Too deep to move the RV we hoped it would stop
It didn’t
John emptied the contents of the big cooler and stored 3 of the 12 batteries
The rest he moved higher up along with anything else
We used plastic bins turned upside down on the bed with the couch cushions on top
Me, the dogs and cats stayed in the back
John kept stowing things
The water kept rising in the RV and when it hit my chest I called 911
Emergency rescues were not happening
We were out of realistic escapes
THOUGHT WE ALL WERE GOING TO DROWN
John was hoping the RV would float
Too heavy with full tanks
I called 911 again
No rescue possible
Then the water went down an inch and continued to recede
We slept in the drenched RV on those couch cushions with the pets
Nothing dry to cover up with except a pair of rain pants and a long, very narrow piece of fabric
It was a long night
The next morning we went into the house to see the damage
Everything had turned every which way, the refrigerator was on its back
The water went 6 inches from the ceiling
Photo
The fire department came out to check on us
The Sheriff’s Dept. came as well
WE ARE HOMELESS
-Cherie Rehkopf

Tiffany is a Marine veteran. She is married to Dave who is an Air Force veteran. They have 2 boys, Oliver, who is 2 and Elliott, who is 7 months. 
On November 6th Tiffany and Dave lost their home and all theirs, and the boys belongings in a house fire. 
Tiffany’s story: 
We have been unpacking things to put away in the cabinets after we got the new appliances. We just kept throwing the empty boxes out back. Around 2:50 I was standing in the dining room starting to unpack another box when I heard a weird crackle noise. I looked at the back door and noticed a very orange color. I opened the door and got ambushed by flames. I tried swatting in the fire hoping to knock the boxes away from the house. I noticed it was too big and too hot so I screamed “daddy”. He ran out the door and started kicking the boxes away from the house when he turned and realized that the back side of the house was consumed in fire and the attic was already engulfed. He screamed for me to get the boys out of the house. I ran inside and snatched Elliott out of his bassinet and Oliver out of his crib. Dave started screaming asking where our fire extinguishers were and I told him in the closet. I ran the babies across the street to the neighbors and then ran back to the house to grab the other fire extinguisher…. It was defective and did not work. I later found the one my husband grabbed was also defective and spray for less than 3 seconds before quitting. My dad told me to get out but I kept screaming call 911 and find Biscuit. All of our animals were taken out by our neighbors but we couldn’t find Biscuit. The neighbor ran over and started spraying the house with the water house. My dad grabbed ours and started spraying too but it was too late. The entire attic and roof was engulfed and smoke was barreling out. I kept trying to find a way to run back inside to find Biscuit but I couldn’t see and couldn’t breath. When EMS arrived I kept screaming to please find my dog. It is still undetermined what the exact cause of the fire was but it’s heavily leaning towards electrical. All I could do is stand and watch smoke barrel out from the top of the roof and then see the roof go up in complete flames. We lost absolutely everything. But I am so thankful for our neighbors for helping us get our boys and our animals out. 
Biscuit: 
After the fire was somewhat contained they performed a search and rescue. Biscuit had been inside for an hour or more. I was just standing there in disbelief, shaken, in shock, when everyone pointed towards the house. Biscuit was being carried out by a fireman and he was ALIVE. The scream I let out is heart wrenching. He was checked out by EMS and highly recommended to get a bath asap. He was soaked and completely covered in soot. They found him hiding in our closet in some clothes. Our room took the most damage. I wanted to be absolutely sure he was okay so I took him to the ER vet. We were very hopeful and in high spirits. His O2 levels were good. But when they ran blood work he had an alarming amount of CO2 in his blood. I had to make a decision either to let him go or perform CPR. I just kept begging for them to do whatever they needed to save my dog. Last night was critical and it was unsure if he would make it through the night….. BUT HE DID. I had to pick him up at the ER vet and get him to his normal vet where he stayed all day for fluids and observation. He was allowed to come home this evening and will have to return in the morning for another day of fluids and monitoring. As long as everything stays stable then he will be completely out of the woods. For tonight he is home and getting extra snuggles and love. 
My daughter and her husband have work so hard to provide a great life for their boys. This tragedy is a nightmare that I wish we could all wake up from. I stood with my daughter as she watched her house crumble to the ground and she screamed in despair. The important thing is she got her babies out, the 2 legged and the 4 legged. 
Everything list is just material and can be replaced. But as we all know the material is not so easy to replace and though insurance will eventually (maybe) cover it they are having to foot a lot of money upfront. They are staying with Tiffany’s father and have had to get bottles, diapers, formula, clothes, beds, the essentials. 
I am hoping that we can raise money for them to help with some of the money and being able to get what they need. Their home is a total loss and will be temporarily staying with her dad for a year at least. Not to mention the increasing vet bill to keep Biscuit alive, he is around $2k right now. The emergency vet holds Biscuit overnight and he goes to his primary vet during the day. The emergency vet is charging but the primary vet wants no payment. 
If you can help in anyway we thank you from the bottoms of our hearts. Times are so very hard for everyone and even a share or a prayer is substantial for this wonderful family. 
Tiffany is the one who has always stepped up and went above and beyond to help anyone and everyone in need. We have told her it’s our turn to take care of her. 
Thank you so much and truly, truly we appreciate you.

It is with a heavy heart that we share the unexpected passing of William Kelly Homer, our beloved Son, father, fiancé, grandson, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend of so many. William was born July 21, 1988 to Tammy Shupp and Kelly Lipsie. His family and friends are both devastated and shocked by his death. He lived passionately every day of his thirty-four years.
William will be missed deeply by his Mother Tammy Shupp and Stepfather Troy Breyfogle, his Daughter Audri Homer, his Father Leon Shupp and Stepmother Roxanne Shupp, his Fiancé Rion Curry, his Father Kelly Lipsie and Stepmother Dixie Lipsie, his Brother Guideon Quinn, his Sister Maria Quinn, his Grandfathers, his many Uncles, Aunts, Cousins, and friends.
William was born in Steamboat Springs, Colorado, and raised in Oak Creek and Steamboat Springs. He attended both SoRoCo and Steamboat Springs schools. In his childhood he treasured spending many of his summers with his beloved Grandmother and Grandfather in California camping, going to the beach, exploring and traveling to different areas. 
Over the course of his life he ran many of his own automotive repair businesses, plowed snow, ran heavy equipment, worked in the oil fields, worked alongside his friends, and fought wildland fires. His passions were being in the great outdoors, snowmobiling, riding atvs, camping, gaming, golfing, exploring, hunting, boating, traveling, driving his treasured trucks, playing pool, listening to music, being with family, his Daughter, his Fiancé, his beloved dog Poobie, and his cherished friends. 
William could accomplish anything he set his mind to do. He was always making everyone laugh with his goofy sense of humor and always tried to be the friend that he would want for himself. His antics were legendary and those who knew him have their own stories to tell. He said what he meant and meant what he said. 
Though he had an adventurous spirit he never would move very far from his Mother. He always felt it was his responsibility to be her fierce protector. He was her best friend, confidant, rock, and would move mountains just to make sure she had what was in his ability to give. In Routt County, he found his passion for the great outdoors often spending his younger years camping and riding with his family and friends. He became a dad to his Daughter, Audri, at the age of 27 and fell in love immediately. He was excited to share the world he knew with her and teach her everything he had learned in his short life. He tried to protect and shelter her from everything that could possibly hurt her. She has inherited the very best parts of William and through her, his family and friends will make sure his bright light and legacy lives on.
To know him is to know one of the finest humans on earth. William had a presence that lit up a room. He was stubborn, hard-headed and set in his ways, but if you took the time to really get to know him and peel away the exterior layers, you would find he had a brilliant mind, he was sensitive, and he was passionate about family and the people and things he truly loved.  His personality and laugh were infectious. William was always trying to be better, do better and learn more about everything. William was always making friends wherever he went. He was a stranger to no one and found great purpose sharing in the successes, joys, and challenges of those around him. William was authentically and wholeheartedly there for those in his life. He fully enjoyed what he did and those he met. He made the time to show up for everyone who reached out, providing caring, trustworthy, and sound counsel. Our dear friend and colleague Huaxi Xu passed away on Oct. 14, 2022.

We watched Huaxi’s career flourished over the years, from that young bright postdoc in the lab of Nobel Laureate Dr. Paul Greengard at Rockefeller University, to the professor and director of Neurodegenerative Disease Program at Sanford-Burnham Biomedical Institute and later professor at Xianmen University Medical College.  Huaxi has published more than 180 papers and received numerous awards during this time.  As the co-founder and co-editor in chief of Molecular Neurodegeneration since its inception in 2006, he worked tirelessly to make this journal a highly visible platform for scientists from different parts of the world to share their latest findings. Huaxi’s proudest accomplishment is perhaps the many students and postdocs he guided through their early scientific careers and now are contributing to many aspects of biomedical research.  He will be sorely missed by his friends, colleagues and Alzheimer research community.  
Huaxi left behind two young daughters: Madeline 6 and Adele 10.  To lose their beloved father at such a young age is truly heartbreaking.  This fundraising campaign is for them – to support their education and to bring them closer to their father through the love and care of his many friends as they grow up. This summer our friend and colleague Anthony Hendrie told us that he had been diagnosed with Stage IV Melanoma. It was devastating news for his friends and family. Anthony epitomized the tireless colleague, and we aren’t referring only to his work ethic. He was tirelessly optimistic; he always greeted you with a smile and a “Hey, Mate.” He was tirelessly kind; the first to jump in and help when asked. He was tirelessly sincere; he earned deep respect and trust from those around him. He was tireless in all the ways that really matter, and took on his challenge in the same fashion, with a courage that we could only hope to summon under the same circumstances. In speaking with some of his closest colleagues last month, Anthony shared laughs, his desire to catch up in person over a glass of wine, and his thanks for all the calls, cards, emails, and texts that so many had sent along, adding, “Ah, Mate, you have no idea how much it all means to me.” The outpouring of support that came to Anthony was entirely expected given the kind of colleague and friend he was to the people whose lives intersected with his life.
In the last few months, Anthony’s grace belied the difficulties he faced. He passed away Thursday, November 10th, at the age of 53. Our most heartfelt condolences go to his wife Tricia, daughter Sienna (11), and son James (8), his parents, siblings, and all his family. We want to share a few more words about Anthony, in tribute to him, and above all we want to show his family the support they need and deserve. The last few months brought extensive medical bills so anything we can do to help the family address these and future challenges would truly be the most appropriate way to honor Anthony.
One of the best descriptions of Anthony would be “family man,” and how that family came to be was one of the great stories Anthony loved sharing. Anthony’s background jumped out right away. He was Australian, and proudly so. As many of his friends know, at a certain point years ago he decided he was ready to head back to his homeland. He booked a flight, made all arrangements, and went out to celebrate the close of his chapter here in the United States with friends just a few days before his planned departure. As fate would have it, he met the love of his life that very evening. They went on a date the next day. Needless to say, Anthony cancelled his flight. Marriage soon followed, along with two beautiful children, a continued career here in the U.S., and, eventually, American citizenship. Anthony could not have been prouder of his heritage as well as of his adopted home, and his family, both in Australia and in the US. He was full of wonderful stories about family and friends, the most important pieces of his life, and there was no greater pleasure than sitting down with Anthony and swapping these stories.
Anthony supported so many people and causes over the years, and would literally give the shirt off his back for family, friends and colleagues. Let’s raise a glass (on this occasion, it has to be Shiraz) to our mate Anthony, and continue our love and support for him and his family.
Thank you

Hey ya'll, my name is Hannah, & I don't know how to do this, so bear with me here. 
I'm fundraising to save Shamrock, my friend Haylee's horse. Shamrock, or Sham as most of us call him, is a 5-year-old Quarter Horse and the sweetest horse you will ever meet.
Haylee has raised him since he was weaned. She has poured every ounce of her heart and soul into training him & making him the fantastic horse he is today. In return, Sham has brought her solace & joy through some of the darkest times of her life, many of those being in the last year. She has faced so much adversity, it's a wonder she's still standing, & Sham has been there every step of the way.
Then, a couple of months ago, Sham started to drop on his topline, & it seemed overnight he lost all of the muscle on his back end. Haylee tried everything she knew to bring it back, but nothing worked. He started to stumble at random when he walked. She had a gut feeling about what was wrong with Sham but couldn't get an equine vet out to see him until last month. This is what he looks like now:
They drew some blood to run the tests Haylee asked for to get confirmation of her suspicions, but deep down, we all thought, "it can't be". Wishful thinking, I suppose.
Fast forward to yesterday, November 7th, Haylee & I are limping down the road in her truck, pulling 2 of her clients' horses in the trailer, & she finally gets the return call from the vet about Sham's test results. She was correct; Sham has EPM. 
EPM (or Equine Protozoal Myeloencephalitis) is, in short, a neurological disease. More than 50% of all horses in the U.S. may have been exposed to the organism that causes EPM. This organism is a parasite called Sarcocystis neurona. The disease is not transmitted from horse to horse but is actually spread from multiple animals through the Opossum, or more specifically, their feces, which can contaminate hay & grass, etc. Once ingested, the sporocysts migrate from the intestinal tract into the bloodstream & cross the blood/brain barrier. There they begin to attack the horse's central nervous system. Onset may be slow or sudden. If left undiagnosed & untreated, EPM can cause devastating and lasting neurological damage. Symptoms range from abnormal sweating to seizures & paralysis of the muscles of the eyes, face or mouth.
Thankfully, EPM is treatable. The sooner treatment begins, the better the horse's chances are for recovery. 60-70% of EPM cases aggressively treated show significant or complete reversal of symptoms.  ( Source: https://aaep.org/horsehealth/epm-understanding-debilitating-disease )
After having had several conversations over the last 36 hours with people with horses with EPM, it sounds as if the younger the horse, the better the results.
So why am I telling you all this, and what am I asking for?
Treatment for Sham will be expensive. For two rounds of treatment & all of the supplements needed in addition & maintenance medications for about six months after initial treatment, it will cost roughly $2500.00. 
Haylee is self-employed, running a boarding facility for 15 horses in addition to her own, & the price of hay & feed has skyrocketed this year. She teaches riding, roping & barrel racing lessons to support herself. Let me put it this way; Haylee is the hardest-working woman I have ever come across in my entire life. She gives and gives and gives of herself until there's nothing left. She has done more for me in the past year than I can explain, and she probably doesn't even know it. That's just who Haylee is. Bottom line, she cannot afford his treatment.
Because she cannot afford treatment, Haylee has two choices here, but if you asked her, she would say she doesn't have a choice. She could let him live his life & get progressively worse until he one day passes away. Or, she could put him down out of mercy, and for Haylee, that's a no-brainer.
But because of who she is, what she does for all of us at the barn, the life she has led and the insurmountable troubles she has faced, I cannot sit back and watch her lose him.  
Haylee's unending courage, perseverance and flat-out FIGHT is rare in this current day and age. Sham is the one thing that has been hers from the start, the one thing that brings her peace and solace. Sham makes all of it worth it, and I cannot let her lose him.
So I'm asking you to please help. Please show my friend that there is kindness in this world and that what she has with Sham matters. 
Any blessing you can give will be beyond appreciated. If I could pay it all, I would; Sham is worth it. Please help us save Sham.

But, what she encountered were two 14-year-old pugs in pretty bad shape, pugs who were possibly going to be left behind—she didn’t know. They were dirty and lying in urine. Toenails were so long they curled under and some punctured and grew into the toe pads. The little girl (pictured right) couldn't use her back legs and her feet dragged backwards behind her when she struggled to move around. The little boy (pictured left) has a large growth on his underside (now determined a skin tag), some small growths on his face, what appears to be an ulceration in his eye, and he is about 12-13 pounds overweight.
Kimberly D. is our neighbor whose heart poured into this situation, and she knew she had to get them out of there. She reached out to me because of our rescue efforts and she has fostered for us before. Kimberly spoke with the dogs' owner and visited a number of times during week begging to let her help. The dogs were miserable and didn't deserve to be in such awful conditions. Their mama was so torn over the situation... she felt horrible and she loves her dogs very much, but had become overwhelmed.
Before we judge the dogs' owner, please understand she has gone through some very challenging times and life fell apart. The dogs didn't get the care they needed the last couple years but she loves them dearly. With the compassion extended by Kimberly, the woman agreed to let Kimberly help, and even keep the dogs, or euthanize if needed -- but she wanted the opinion of a veterinarian before she would agree to euthanasia.
Kimberly picked up the dogs Thursday and their owner cried with sorrow and with appreciation. She didn't understand why Kimberly was pushing so hard to help ... but we know why ... it's because God sent her. The dogs needed her, and their mama needed her.
AJ and Ellie both got baths on Thursday, so they smelled fresh and clean, and they likely felt a sense of confusion, yet comfort in the plush soft and clean beds where they rested at Kimberly's home. During the night hours, AJ presented a significant cough, seeming problematic so Kimberly rushed him to the vet. Emergency exam and diagnostics were $905. It was determined his cough is likely a collapsed trachea, for which not much can be done. A full blood panel was done and all his values look pretty darn good, especially for an overweight 14-year-old dog.
Ellie had been scheduled for a vet appointment Friday. Upon exam and some initial testing, it was determined she could (should) be euthanized, or $2000-3000 could be spent on testing and diagnostics, but nothing really could be done to help her at her very senior age. Kimberly took the dogs to the park yesterday and they were so excited to be there ... but then Ellie tried to run and she just couldn't. She was frustrated and mad.... so Kimberly swept her up and got her home to rest in comfort.
The vet, who agreed euthanasia would be best for Ellie, required owner permission to put Ellie to sleep; so with a phone call, the owner agreed to come. She was able to be with Ellie as Ellie was sent to peaceful slumber, as Kimberly stood near with her heart breaking. Their mama was so heartbroken but was able to come to peace with letting Ellie go. I never even met the dogs, and my heart is breaking... my tears are falling. Kimberly has been crying all day :(
Before Ellie crossed the Rainbow Bridge, she had a most pampered and loving day at Kimberly's home, knowing she was loved and that someone cared for this sweet baby's life.
For AJ, he's staying at Kimberly's house for now. Kimberly is actually one of our fosters and had to get some weight off of a foster dog this past summer (she ended up adopting 10-year-old Gigi). So, she's a pro at home-cooking and calorie counting for dogs now! Kimberly plans on doing some healthy, low-fat cooking for AJ so he can lose some weight and feel the best he can.
In the meantime, we would like to know if anyone would like to give AJ an amazing home for whatever time he has left.  He's very loving and just needs some special attention ... he's now lost his mama, and he's lost his life-long fur-gal, Ellie.  Please let me know if you have a soft spot for senior dogs and would like to take him under wing.  
Also, I would like to generate a little community fundraiser to help with reimbursing Kimberly for the $2065 she spent helping these two dogs, which includes a visit for AJ on 10/31 to test his eyes, get him vaccinated, and get him some further testing. The doctor said surprisingly, this guy is in pretty good shape and will have some happy times ahead.
If you would like to contribute towards Ellie & AJ's vet bills, it would be so appreciated. You may contribute via venmo ( @sherry-petta-1 ) or here on gofundme. I’m including images of the three invoices – Kimberly has already paid them, but we’re hoping with a community effort, this doesn’t all lie on her shoulders.
Very often, rescue is happy ... bubbly dogs who get to start out a new and amazing life. Also very often, we encounter situations like this where you simply need to help, even if the dog doesn’t have a lot of time left ... they deserve to have it be the best it can be. ❤
My HUGE thank-you goes out to Kimberly who went above and beyond for these beautiful senior babies, and to all of you who so often lend a helping hand to the rescue with unexpected vet bills.  Thank you all. ❤
